chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the woman whose husband performs li'an with her, and they are separated; to whom is her child attributed? He said: 'To his mother.'

key_terms.يُلاَعِنُهَا: He performs li'an with her (mutual imprecation)

ai.seo_question: Who is the child attributed to after li'an in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *li'an* (mutual imprecation) detailed in Surah An-Nur, this hadith clarifies the lineage (*nasab*) of offspring born after the separation, attributing them solely to the mother. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it severs the paternal link for inheritance and marriage prohibitions, distinguishing it from cases where the husband's claim is not formally sworn. The narration underscores the finality of the imprecation ceremony in determining maternal lineage when paternity is disputed.
